body: 🎧 da — James is here. two minutes, in the car, both of you. he gets his first three Tamil words — and podhum is yours to back up. வாங்க.
memo_script:
வணக்கம், James.

I'm Anna. I'm from Coimbatore, and for a few months now I've been teaching your brother Tamil. He didn't tell you. That was rather the point.

So — வணக்கம். Vanakkam. That's your first word, and it's the only greeting you need. Hands together. It works at a shop, at a temple, at someone's mother's front door.

Two more and you can survive a Tamil house. நன்றி — nandri — thank you. And போதும் — podhum — enough. That second one matters more than you'd think. When the aunty puts a third helping of rice on your plate and you genuinely cannot continue: போதும். Say it warmly. She will ignore you. Say it again anyway.

Andrew — போதும் is yours. You fired that one cold. Back me up.

வாங்க, James. Welcome. Have a good evening, both of you.
